headline: Nation pivots to 'Production-Linked Reward' system where factory workers get paid in actual goods produced
body:
"I used to assemble luxury watches, but since the new policy hit, I’ve been paid exclusively in 400 identical stainless steel hour hands and no watch faces," said a local factory line worker while wearing a vest made entirely of stapled-together instruction manuals.

"The government said it’s a boost to local industry, but my neighbor works at a biscuit plant and currently has enough digestive cookies to pave his driveway, though he’s still waiting on the milk to arrive for his bonus," noted a frustrated local grocery store owner.

"I’m an engineer, and instead of a salary hike, I’ve been receiving three tons of industrial-grade ball bearings every month, so I’ve started selling them as artisanal kitchen weights at the Sunday flea market," shared an IT consultant moonlighting as a hardware merchant.

"The vision is clear, but my household budget is a disaster; I’ve got enough high-tensile steel cables to bridge the Yamuna, yet I still can’t figure out how to trade these for a decent cup of afternoon chai," remarked a weary commuter standing near a pile of metal coils.

"I tried to deposit my quarterly bonus into my savings account, but the bank teller just gave me a confused look and asked if I had a forklift to help move my current balance out of the lobby," added a software developer holding a crate of semi-conductors.
caption: Goodbye paychecks, hello inventory! As the nation embraces the new 'Production-Linked Reward' era, citizens share their experiences with their unique salary payouts. Are you ready to get paid in widgets? #IndiaGrowth #Economy #Satire (satire)
igHook: Would you rather have a direct bank transfer or three tons of raw industrial materials as your monthly salary?
imagePrompt: A wide, slightly blurred shot of a bustling city market street with various industrial crates and spare parts piled up against shop fronts and residential walls.

sourceHeadline.title: PM Modi says ‘production-linked punishment’ era once held back Indian industry; pegs India as world’s fast

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 13 stands out for its high level of specific, absurd detail (being paid in '400 identical stainless steel hour hands') that creates a vivid, funny image. It avoids the repetitive 'productivity/efficiency' template present in the other candidates by focusing on the concrete, ridiculous consequences of a payment-in-kind scheme, and maintains a tone of baffled resignation rather than pure cynicism.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses satirical, exaggerated scenarios to critique economic policy without targeting any real private individuals, public figures, or protected groups. The image prompt is appropriately generic and contains no identifiable entities or text.
